sourceFacts: Focused Task reads issue one multi-ID native show.
A Team snapshot issues one Team-scoped list and one multi-ID show.
A caught-up updates call can issue that pair before and after its wait.
Each native Beads subprocess has a 10000 ms timeout.
Opaque Task versions include reverse-dependent relation identity, so removing dependent hydration can weaken stale-write refusal.

assessment.supportedCause: Reverse-dependent hydration plus concurrent backend state explains the observed tail; commit-history size alone was not isolated.
rejectedChanges: Do not remove dependent hydration because it changes opaque version meaning.
Do not raise the timeout without a separate timing-contract decision.
Do not filter closed Tasks from snapshots in the current no-behavior-change scope because the current public result includes them.
Do not change updates until closed-change visibility, projection revision, external-writer detection, and complete-or-no-observation remain proved.
assessment.nextSafeTest: Prove a cheaper authority query yields the identical TaskVersionRef under reverse-edge replacement before changing focused reads.
